summary: Timeboxed access to encrypted KV-key checksums for targeted remediation of customer output discrepancy
description:
Background: BrightCart reported a small set of customer complaints where the model returned legacy payment token formats in 3 unique sessions over the past 48 hours. Initial triage indicates the routing and model versioning are correct, but the customer has supplied matching request IDs and a suspected KV-cache collision window that might have replayed a stale prefix for these sessions.

Impact: Business-facing (BrightCart enterprise). 3 affected user sessions; potential PII exposure of masked payment tokens (masked but format-leaking). Customer expects a remediation plan and a scoped transcript to perform a rectification for impacted end-users. No broad production outage.

Request: Approve timeboxed, read-only access to encrypted KV-key checksums + minimal session metadata (no raw user payloads) for the three specified request IDs to validate whether a stale prefix replay occurred. The data requested is the HMAC keyed checksum of KV-keys and the timestamp window they were active. This allows verification without transmitting plaintext user data.

Justification: The checksum approach preserves data minimization (we do not request plaintext payloads). Customer requires evidence to support their remediation and user notifications. Legal and Privacy have preliminarily confirmed this is a proportional request if proper safeguards are in place.

Data minimization plan: Only return checksums and metadata: kv_key_hmac, key_active_from, key_active_to, internal_node_id, request_id. Redaction: strip any IP, auth headers, and raw prompt/response content before any handoff. No long-term persistence allowed; snapshot will be deleted after verification and audit log entry.

Access controls: Two-person control required (SRE + Privacy reviewer). Access will be read-only via ephemeral audit account with KMS-wrapped session token. All activity logged in the audit trail. Access window requested: 2 hours. Storage retention: 72 hours encrypted, then automatic delete.

Timeline: Need approval by 2026-03-14 (EOD) to meet customer remediation timeline; extraction can be executed 2026-03-15 09:00-11:00 UTC.

Approvers requested: Security (Data Access Approver), Privacy Counsel, SRE oncall.

Deliverables: 1) CSV of checksums+metadata (HMAC only), 2) verification note stating whether checksum correlation indicates stale-prefix replay, 3) signed access audit entry.

investigation_notes: Triage performed 2026-03-13 by SRE: located three sessions with request_ids: rc-20260311-8a7, rc-20260312-33f, rc-20260312-7d2. All routed to redwood-open-7b in us-east. No 5xx or throttling recorded around those timestamps.

Checked model rollout logs: client pinned to rwx-compat-13b v2026-03-01. No recent rollouts overlapping timeframe. Serving runtime trace shows brief KV eviction spike on node n-us-east-07 at 2026-03-12T02:11Z (GC window). Hypothesis: transient eviction caused lookup fallback to stale prefix on that node.
Risk assessment: Low probability of large-scale exposure, but high customer trust impact. Need cryptographic verification (HMAC checksums) to confirm if session KV keys matched stale entries.

Extraction plan drafted: run checksum extractor against node n-us-east-07 for specified keyspace and time window; produce HMAC values using audit-only HMAC key stored in KMS; don't emit plaintext keys or payloads.
resolution: Awaiting approvals from Security and Privacy. No extraction executed yet. Next step post-approval: schedule two-person extraction window and provide CSV output plus audit log reference.
